fact: There is no `validator` agent type: VALIDATE is always run by the orchestrator itself (trust nothing, never delegate quality gates or trust a subagent's report), so a validator agent would never be spawned.
recommendation: Do not add a validator role or delegate VALIDATE; keep it orchestrator-run in orchestrated-execution and external-tools.

fact: The 3-attempt Recovery Protocol and coder model escalation apply only to VALIDATE failures; review rounds follow the severity-gated rule in guides/delivery-scope.md (SAFETY_CAP 10). Design persona briefs are checklists only; agents/design-reviewer.md overrides their output format.
recommendation: Change review-iteration behaviour in guides/delivery-scope.md (and the gates' copied rule lines), not in Recovery Protocol text; change design-review output shape in design-reviewer.md and the gate schemas, not in persona files.

fact: VALIDATE attempts count consecutive failed VALIDATE runs and reset to 0 (and drop the retry:N label) on a VALIDATE PASS, because review rounds are variable (severity rule, cap 10) and a never-reset counter would escalate a progressing work unit.
recommendation: Keep the VALIDATE limit per run of consecutive failures; bound the review loop only via the severity rule. See decision-ms-review-vs-validate-limits.

fact: A review gate passes only when a fresh round has no blocker: yes finding (or via rule line 5's downgrade). Escalating to the human never approves: options are Revise, Narrow scope, Defer or Cancel, and changed work gets a fresh round.
recommendation: Never describe an escalated gate as approved or offer override/proceed-anyway/known-risk options; after the human's choice, re-run a fresh review round and report PASS only when every reviewer passes.
